definitions.decline: the line is still printed in the last year, its own peak reached at least $10,000, and the mean of its last 2 printed years is at or under 50% of that peak
definitions.permanent: the line’s last funded year is followed only by printed zeros, for as long as the line appears at all
definitions.rename: two differently-spelled lines carrying the identical value in every fiscal year they share, where the older one stops first
definitions.returned: the same line carries a value above zero again in a later year
definitions.spelling_candidate: a line stops, and a line spelled almost the same for the same school starts after it. Ours, and a candidate: there is no shared year, so no arithmetic settles it
definitions.twin: the same, where BOTH labels run to the last year of the series — two labels on identical figures, which is not evidence of a rename
definitions.vanished: the line stops appearing in the book altogether
definitions.zeroing: the line carries a value above zero in one year and a printed zero in the next, with both years present in the book

gaps.closes: the district’s own crosswalk from the FY2022 budget-book line list to the FY2023 presentation, or the MUNIS year-end expense report (glytdbud, period 13) for the school department for those years, which is keyed on accounts rather than on printed line names.
gaps.what: Whether a school line that stops appearing in the district’s book stopped being funded
gaps.why: A line can leave the book because the money stopped, or because the book changed shape. Both look identical: an absence. Between FY2022 and FY2023 the restated series moves from one district budget book to another, the number of printed lines falls by about a third, and the reported total RISES — so the lines that stop appearing at that boundary cannot have taken their money with them. At least five of the disappearances are established renames, two lines differing only in spelling and carrying the identical value in every year they share (`Maint. of Buildings/Contrcted Services` and `Maint. of Buildings/Contracted Services`). Nothing published maps the older line list onto the newer one, so for any individual line, absence is a fact about the document and not about the service.

gaps.closes: a district budget book for FY2026 or later printing the full line list with prior-year columns, in the same shape as `fy24-approved-budget`.
gaps.what: Which school lines stopped being funded in FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025
gaps.why: The restated figures for those years come from the FY27 budget projection workbooks, which print a shorter line list and almost no zeros. Not one line in them goes from funded in one year to a printed zero in the next — so the measurement this project can make for FY2015 through FY2022 has no evidence at all for the three most recent years. That is a property of which document restates which year, not a finding that nothing stopped.

gaps.closes: a filled-position list, or payroll by position rather than by name.
gaps.what: Whether a budgeted position was filled
gaps.why: A budget line is money the town has to raise, not a person in a chair. A line funded all year for a post vacant half of it looks identical on the page to one that was filled. **Bounded, not settled**: the rosters show who was printed, which narrows the question without answering it.

gaps.closes: the MUNIS year-end expense report (glytdbud, period 13) for the school department for each year wanted, which is the same report we already hold for FY2026.
gaps.what: What the schools actually spent, per line, in any year before FY2026
gaps.why: The district publishes a column headed ACTUAL in its forward budget books, and twelve years of it load as `budget_figure` where stage='restated' — the stage was called `actual` until 7 September 2026, and the rename is the point. Those are RESTATEMENTS — a prior year re-presented inside a document written by the party that spent it — and `document-basis.csv` classifies all sixteen source documents behind them as `restatement` (14) or `forward` (2). None is a ledger. The archive holds ten ledger documents in total, and the only ones reaching school general-fund spending are one quarter of FY23 and FY2026 period 12. So the question 'did the schools spend what they budgeted' cannot be settled before FY2026 from anything published: both sides of the comparison come out of the same budget book, and a restatement cannot show money moved between lines mid-year because approved transfers do not appear in a budget document.

said.quote: Ana Lockwood seeks information about guidance counselors. Dr. Jodi Fortuna states there are only guidance counselors at the high school.
said.why: Three of the four guidance counsellor lines stop appearing in the district’s book after FY2022 and the middle school line is still funded in FY2025. A budget line is not a filled post, and this is the two halves sitting side by side.

said.quote: the remaining $17,000 will be dedicated to contracted professional development
said.why: Every PER-SCHOOL professional development line in the district’s book is printed at zero from FY2021 onward, while the district-wide line rises. In FY2026 the Superintendent reports professional development being paid for out of a DESE grant as well. Three facts side by side; nothing here says any one of them caused another.

said.quote: Dr. Jodi Fortuna and the other presenters do not suggest cutting social workers.
said.why: Said in the same passage, in the same meeting, about the neighbouring line.
